response.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating

assumptions.assumption: Expensive means replacement_cost >= 20.99 (the cutoff is inclusive). Since replacement_cost has two decimals, a film at exactly 20.99 counts as expensive.
The second average is computed per film as rental_rate / rental_duration (cost per rental day), then averaged within each rating. This is not the ratio of the two averages.

alternatives.interpretation: Expensive means strictly greater than 20.99, so films at exactly 20.99 are excluded.
alternatives.sql: SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating

response.note: AVG ignores NULLs, so missing length values are skipped.
